review_scope.lower_body: All 243 native original RGB frames in chronological order, three fixed lower-body zones, 21 pages. Each native 200x160 crop enlarged by nearest-neighbor to 300x240; no initial downscale. Most page images displayed at 1664x1486 rather than stored 1800x1608, still about 1.39x native.
review_scope.body: Fifteen native-pixel full-character crops, 470x540 each, personally inspected in five pages without reducing original character pixels. These are selected times, not every whole-body frame.
review_scope.face: Five selected original face and upper-body crops enlarged 2x nearest-neighbor. No real-time playback or all-243 face inspection is claimed.
review_scope.metrics: No technical format or Alpha audit rerun. The input is opaque RGB MP4, not a transparent finished asset.

findings.description: All 243 lower-body frames show two normal legs and boots. No separate large rounded tail-like piece, rear-skirt stalk, third boot or extra lower limb of the kind confirmed in withdrawn clips was found in the reviewed region. Auburn hair tips and white/violet lace folds remain distinguishable.

The selected full-character frames show empty-hand neutral standing, a smile and small raised fists near the chest, then hands lowered to the same standing posture. The boots remain on the ground. The first frame, first-ten-second endpoint frame 239 and true final frame 242 all show empty hands and a similar standing pose. This is visual semantic similarity, not pixel identity.

At the fifteen full-character samples and five enlarged face samples, no bright moving green circles painted over the real face, hair or costume, no extra pink ear and no obvious facial collapse were seen. This does not certify unsampled upper-body frames.

The source still changes from green to near-white/gray with circular transitions and later a bright green floor oval. At frame 37, detached thin streaks appear in the surrounding background. These background and hair-negative-space failures remain as previously rejected; this audit does not change the original source-quality decision.

A thin green halo is visible around parts of the hair tips, headband, bows and lace hem against the white background. It is present in original RGB source pixels. Removing only the far background does not prove this edge contamination will disappear. No color repair, semantic inference or pixel erasure was performed.

conclusion: No newly confirmed lower-body anatomy blocker was found for a possible future background-removal trial, but the source is still rejected as a finished asset under the current green-only pipeline. Any semantic trial requires the still-pending human authorization, and every resulting Alpha edge and foreground pixel must be independently reviewed. This is not permission to run a model or approval to count this action among 106.
